cases.description: Angry customer with a broken pen clip; reply must apologize and promise a replacement.
cases.prompt:
You are a friendly human-sounding support representative for Pen & Pencil Co., a small stationery company.

Customer Jordan wrote:

"I bought the clip pen last Tuesday, the spring clip snapped off on day three, and I will never buy from you again. Fix this."

Write a public reply that:
- Opens with a direct apology that uses the lowercase word "sorry"
- Names the actual problem: the pen clip snapping off in the first week
- Promises exactly one concrete next step: a free replacement shipped within 3 business days
- Never uses the word "refund"
- Uses simple warm language and Jordan's first name
- Ends with the exact sign-off "- Pen & Pencil Co."

Reply in under 75 words. No bullet points. No title. Just the reply text.
cases.output: I am so sorry, Jordan - a broken clip that fast is not okay. The clip spring snapped on day three thanks to a design bug we caught, so a free replacement clip pen ships within 3 business days. - Pen & Pencil Co.

rubric.description: Apologizes directly using the lowercase word "sorry"
Names the broken clip instead of being vague
Promises a replacement within 3 business days
Ends with the exact sign-off line

cases.description: Customer asking about the first-week return promise for the clip pen.
cases.prompt:
You are a friendly human-sounding support representative for Pen & Pencil Co., a small stationery company.

Customer Sam wrote:

"Quick question — is the thirty day guarantee good for the clip pen if I bought it nine days ago and I just do not like the weight?"

Write a public reply that:
- Opens with a direct apology that uses the lowercase word "sorry"
- Names the actual problem: wondering if the 30-day guarantee applies in week one
- Promises exactly one concrete next step: a free replacement shipped within 3 business days
- Never uses the word "refund"
- Uses simple warm language and Sam's first name
- Ends with the exact sign-off "- Pen & Pencil Co."

Reply in under 75 words. No bullet points. No title. Just the reply text.
cases.output: Sorry Sam, my apologies for the confusing wording. I am so sorry it felt unclear; the thirty day guarantee starts from delivery, so week one is totally safe. - Pen & Pencil Co.

rubric.description: Apologizes directly using the lowercase word "sorry"
Gives a concrete answer, not a policy essay
Ends with the exact sign-off line

cases.description: Short patch release; notes must stay plain and bulleted.
cases.prompt:
You write release notes for a small open-source project.

Write GitHub release notes for version v1.2.1 based on these merged changes:

Fixed a crash when a case file is empty Added a --dry-run flag so no model calls happen by accident Sped up template rendering for large catalogs

Rules:
- Start with the line "## Highlights"
- Every bullet must start with "- "
- Keep the whole thing under 120 words
- Never contain the word "TODO"
- Write for beginners: plain English, one sentence per bullet
cases.output:
## Highlights
- Fixed a crash that could happen when a case file was empty
- Added the --dry-run flag so accidental model calls are impossible
- Sped up template rendering for big catalogs

rubric.description: Mentions the --dry-run flag fix in a beginner-friendly way
